mechanics: Read the map gate at this+0x38; when it is zero return EAX=0 immediately without touching the map.

Allocate a stack-local cursor initialised to null, then call 0x00e5c780 with the map at this+0x08, the address of the local key holder and the address of that cursor. The port receives a valid, non-null out pointer; nothing is inferred from the call's return register.
Compare the cursor written through the out pointer against the end sentinel at this+0x0c. An end result returns EAX=0 and never calls 0x0059c740.
Otherwise call 0x0059c740 (map find/get) and return the single word stored at the returned slot, so an absent key yields the zero-initialised default value and therefore a null controller.
Epilogue is POP EDI/ESI/ECX, RET 0x4 in both paths.

lower_bound_contract.out_parameter: third stack argument, always a valid address of a caller-owned cursor
lower_bound_contract.cursor_source: the cursor is read back from that out slot, never from the call's return value

lookup_null_behaviour.gate_zero: this+0x38 == 0 short-circuits to null without any map call
lookup_null_behaviour.lower_bound_end: cursor == this+0x0c returns null and skips the find call
lookup_null_behaviour.find_miss: 0x0059c740 yields a zeroed default pair, so the returned controller pointer is null

evidence.observation: LEA EAX,[ESP+0x10] then PUSH EAX, followed by a second PUSH of the key address, proves 0x00e5c780 receives two real stack arguments; the out slot is at [ESP+0x10] and is compared at CMP dword ptr [EAX],EDI.

The routine ends with MOV EAX,[ESP+0x8]; MOV dword ptr [EAX],ECX; RET 0x8, so it returns the out pointer and writes the node through it. The reconstruction therefore reads the cursor back from the out slot.
find returns node+0x14 on a hit and the address of a zeroed default pair on a miss, so the caller's single-word deref is the null path.
30 direct call sites across editor, placement and world helpers.

evidence: 0x00e5c780 stores the found node through [ESP+0x8] and dereferences [ESP+0xc] as the search key, so the native stack order after the receiver is (out, key). The port declaration and both call sites use (map, out, key) with a non-null out pointer and the cursor is read back from that slot.
